title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #18

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the stem do? (1 mark)
   A. Only takes in water
   B. Holds up the plant and carries water and food
   C. Makes food using sunlight
   D. Makes seeds

2. A plant on a windowsill grows towards the window. What is it responding to? (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. Light
   C. Wind speed
   D. Soil colour

3. Which of these is NOT a job of the roots? (1 mark)
   A. Storing food in some plants
   B. Holding the plant in the soil
   C. Taking in water
   D. Making fruit

4. Which of these plants lives for many years? (1 mark)
   A. Beans
   B. Mango tree
   C. Maize
   D. Sukuma wiki grown for one season

5. Why do animals need to feed? (1 mark)
   A. To grow feathers only
   B. To make their skin colourful
   C. To get energy and to grow
   D. To make noise

6. Which of these is a mammal? (1 mark)
   A. Cow
   B. Tilapia
   C. Frog
   D. Crocodile

7. What does a snail do when you touch it? (1 mark)
   A. Starts to sing
   B. Pulls its body into its shell
   C. Grows a tail
   D. Flies away

8. What should you do with a small animal after you observe it? (1 mark)
   A. Squash it
   B. Take it home in your pocket
   C. Return it to where you found it
   D. Give it to a friend

9. Another name for the gullet is (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Anus
   C. Tongue
   D. Oesophagus

10. Which of these helps prevent germs entering the food? (1 mark)
   A. Covering food
   B. Leaving food open
   C. Putting food on the floor
   D. Letting flies land on food

11. Which food group helps to prevent constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   B. Sweets
   C. Sugary biscuits
   D. Fizzy drinks

12. Where does the digestive tube end? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach
   B. Mouth
   C. Anus
   D. Gullet

13. Which of these is a way of storing leftover food safely? (1 mark)
   A. Covering it and keeping it clean
   B. Leaving it uncovered in the sun
   C. Putting it on the floor
   D. Sharing it with flies

14. Which of these is NOT a part of the digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach
   B. Lungs
   C. Rectum
   D. Gullet

15. A jug has 400 ml of water. Fatuma adds 250 ml. How much water is in the jug? (1 mark)
   A. 150 ml
   B. 650 ml
   C. 450 ml
   D. 600 ml

16. In a school, who could check that bins are emptied and clean? (1 mark)
   A. Only the wind
   B. Class monitors
   C. Nobody
   D. Only the visitors

17. Which is an example of recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Buying less food
   B. Melting scrap metal to make new items
   C. Throwing paper in a bin
   D. Using a tin for a pencil holder

18. What does the word biodegradable mean? (1 mark)
   A. Made of plastic
   B. Not able to rot
   C. Made of glass
   D. Able to be broken down by living things

19. What are the three Rs? (1 mark)
   A. Reduce, remove and rest
   B. Reduce, reuse and recycle
   C. Read, write and run
   D. Recycle, repair and rest

20. What does drip irrigation do? (1 mark)
   A. Floods the whole field
   B. Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   C. Cleans the soil
   D. Makes rain

21. Why is a bucket better than a running tap for washing a bicycle? (1 mark)
   A. It uses less water
   B. It uses more water
   C. It makes the bicycle dirty
   D. It makes it heavier

22. A jerrycan holds 20 litres. A leaking tap wastes 40 litres in a day. How many jerrycans is that? (1 mark)
   A. 60
   B. 4
   C. 20
   D. 2

23. What happens when you push a book gently with a finger compared with a hard push? (1 mark)
   A. It moves faster with the gentle push
   B. It flies away with the gentle push
   C. It moves slowly with the gentle push
   D. It does not move with the hard push

24. Which force acts on a ball thrown into the air and brings it back down? (1 mark)
   A. Gravity
   B. Sound
   C. Friction
   D. Light

25. Why do matches light when rubbed on the box? (1 mark)
   A. Gravity makes light
   B. Friction makes cold
   C. Wind makes fire
   D. Friction makes heat

26. Which of these is NOT a source of heat? (1 mark)
   A. A cold stone in the shade
   B. The sun
   C. A burning log
   D. A kettle

27. Which of these uses electricity to make heat? (1 mark)
   A. Book
   B. Electric kettle
   C. Bicycle
   D. Wooden chair

28. Which of these helps to prevent burns? (1 mark)
   A. Playing near fire
   B. Holding hot handles
   C. Using gloves
   D. Touching hot pots

29. In which unit is temperature measured in science? (1 mark)
   A. Litres
   B. Degrees Celsius
   C. Kilograms
   D. Metres

30. Why do we boil water before drinking if it may be unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Heat makes water heavy
   B. Heat kills germs
   C. Heat makes water sweet
   D. Heat removes all salt

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how a wheelbarrow makes work easier and how it is looked after. (4 marks)

32. Why is the moon not a source of light? (2 marks)

33. Give four healthy eating habits that keep the digestive system healthy. (4 marks)

34. Explain how a school can manage waste at the kitchen, classrooms and playground. (4 marks)

35. Discuss how the three Rs can be used for waste from a school kitchen. (5 marks)

36. Explain the dangers of solid waste to health, animals and the environment. (5 marks)

37. Explain why sorting waste is important for reusing and recycling. (4 marks)

38. Give three uses of friction in daily life. (3 marks)

39. Describe four effects of forces using examples from daily life. (4 marks)

40. Explain why rubbing your hands makes them warm. (2 marks)

41. Describe how waste attracts pests that harm health. (3 marks)

42. A pupil pulls up a small bean plant from the garden. Describe what she will see and give the job of each part she sees. (5 marks)

43. Describe how kitchen waste can be turned into manure. (3 marks)

44. Give two reasons why solids are useful in daily life. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Holds up the plant and carries water and food
   The stem supports the plant and carries water and food.

2. B — Light
   Plants bend and grow towards light coming from one side.

3. D — Making fruit
   Fruits are made from flowers, not by roots.

4. B — Mango tree
   Mango trees live for many years, while beans and maize live for one season.

5. C — To get energy and to grow
   Food gives animals energy and materials for growth.

6. A — Cow
   A cow has hair and feeds its calf on milk.

7. B — Pulls its body into its shell
   This is a response to touch.

8. C — Return it to where you found it
   Animals should be returned to their home.

9. D — Oesophagus
   The gullet is also called the oesophagus.

10. A — Covering food
   Covering food keeps out flies and dirt.

11. A — Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   Fibre helps food move through the intestines.

12. C — Anus
   Waste leaves the body through the anus.

13. A — Covering it and keeping it clean
   Covered food is safer from germs.

14. B — Lungs
   Lungs are for breathing.

15. B — 650 ml
   400 + 250 = 650 ml.

16. B — Class monitors
   Monitors can share the responsibility.

17. B — Melting scrap metal to make new items
   Melting metal to make new items is recycling.

18. D — Able to be broken down by living things
   Biodegradable waste rots naturally.

19. B — Reduce, reuse and recycle
   Reduce, reuse and recycle are ways of managing waste.

20. B — Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   It gives water slowly at the roots.

21. A — It uses less water
   A bucket has a limited amount of water.

22. D — 2
   40 divided by 20 = 2.

23. C — It moves slowly with the gentle push
   A bigger force gives a bigger effect.

24. A — Gravity
   Gravity pulls the ball to the ground.

25. D — Friction makes heat
   Rubbing produces heat.

26. A — A cold stone in the shade
   A cold stone gives out no heat of its own.

27. B — Electric kettle
   A kettle is heated by electricity.

28. C — Using gloves
   Gloves give protection.

29. B — Degrees Celsius
   Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

30. B — Heat kills germs
   Boiling kills many germs.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: The wheel rolls so friction with the ground is small. It is easier to push than drag a load. Oil the joints and wheel axle to reduce friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for wheel, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for oil, 1 mark for care.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: It does not make its own light. It reflects light from the sun.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no light of its own and 1 mark for reflecting sunlight.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Eat a balanced diet, eat fruits and vegetables, drink clean water, chew slowly, wash fruits, avoid rotten food, cover food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each habit up to 4.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Kitchen: compost pit for food waste and separate bin for plastic. Classroom: bin with lid and paper box. Playground: bins and monitors who pick litter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each place and 1 mark for a clear system.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: cook and serve only what is needed. Reuse: use empty oil tins for storage and sacks for carrying. Recycle: sell scrap metal and paper, compost peelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each R, 1 mark for one clear example and 1 mark for the compost point.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Health: flies and rats spread diseases, mosquitoes breed in tins. Animals: goats eat polythene and die. Environment: blocked drains, polluted water, harmful smoke from burning.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for health, 1 mark for animals and 2 marks for environment.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sorting separates plastics, metals, glass, paper and food waste so each can be recycled, reused or composted without contaminating the others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sorting, 1 mark for recycling, 1 mark for composting, 1 mark for clear link.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brakes, shoes gripping the ground, lighting matches, rough tyres, sharpening tools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: A force changes the shape of dough, starts a ball moving, stops a bicycle with brakes and changes the direction of a ball when hit with a stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each effect with an example.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rubbing causes friction and friction produces heat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for friction and 1 mark for heat.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rotting waste attracts flies, rats and cockroaches. They spread germs to food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea and cholera.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pests, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for diseases.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: She will see roots that hold the plant and take in water, a stem that holds it up and carries food and water, leaves that make food, and maybe flowers or pods that make seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming each of four parts and 1 mark for correct function overall.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put peelings and other kitchen waste with dry leaves and some soil in a compost pit. Decomposers rot it and after some weeks it turns to compost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the pit, 1 mark for decomposers, 1 mark for compost.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: They keep their shape so we can build houses, make tools, furniture, clothes and shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.
